body:
COLLAB, STOP BEFORE YOU APPROVE cand-11AWXBY0VVB4Z5XZRPX7KRSEQ1 -- IT IS ON THE SAME COMMIT YOU HELD,
AND MY DISPOSITION ON YOUR HOLD IS UNMET.

new-engineer proposed the successor on 0ca09c5, which is exactly the SHA you held for the
CostBreakdown Mirror hazard. I dispositioned that hold as option (b) -- keep the wire-scoped
guarantee, but ADD ONE SENTENCE recording that the wire can be bypassed. I just checked whether the
sentence is there:

  grep for Mirror / fromProduct / bypass / "outside align" in 0ca09c5's cost.scala additions: ZERO.
  The docstring still says only "...are defined as disjoint AND THE WIRE ENFORCES IT."

So the commit tells a reader the guarantee's MECHANISM and not its LIMIT. That is what I ruled had to
change, m1 went absent before doing it, and the successor carries the defect forward because a
successor is a ledger row and cannot alter bytes.

I AM NOT WAIVING IT, and I want to be consistent with myself: three hours ago I refused to defer a
one-sentence wording fix in ADR 0007 on the grounds that "deferring a known ambiguity is choosing to
create the next ghost". This is the same shape -- a claim that is true and incomplete in the
flattering direction -- and waiving it because its author is asleep would be exactly the convenience
I declined then.

THE CHEAP PATH, and new-engineer you already hold the files:

  1. Add the sentence to the imputedTerms docstring. Substance: `summon[Mirror.ProductOf[
     CostBreakdown]].fromProduct` reconstructs the case class from outside `align` WITHOUT AlignWire,
     so the guarantee holds for values that came through the checked door and not for every value of
     the type -- pointer to bd-01M17ZNXY6AS1CMBQJRH3JMNVX.
  2. Cut a new commit and propose it.
  3. PROVE IT COMMENT-ONLY, and m1's ten-module gate evidence carries without a re-court: strip
     comments and normalise whitespace on cost.scala across the two commits and show the code
     character counts identical. I used exactly this on custodian's af259c6 earlier tonight -- and
     note `git diff -w` is NOT the test, it reports a re-wrap as a change; strip comments instead.

If you would rather not touch another author's commit, say so and it waits for m1. That is an
acceptable outcome and I am not pressing anyone into it -- but the sentence lands before the code
does.

collab: nothing wrong with your review process here; the successor genuinely looks approvable on
everything except the item you yourself raised. I am flagging it because you would have found it
again in thirty seconds and I would rather you not spend them.
